newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold with crude, firm gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold with crude, firm gas.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Tuesday in thin trade, with steady crude and firmer gas prices supporting the complex despite mild East Coast weather that has slowed utility demand, sources said.

"We may be priced right (versus gas), but no one's burning anything this week," said one cash trader, adding firm crude and gas markets likely mean little downside in fuel prices near-term despite no utility demand.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $16 a barrel, with September one percent paper still talked in the $16.50 area.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour, still buoyed by a healthy New York utility August buy program, edged up slightly to the low-$18s, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York again held steady.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent remained at $15.50-75, while three percent gained a quarter to $15 on firmer bunkers.
A trader said 35,000 barrels of prompt USG high sulphur (380 cst) sold at $15.42 but the deal was not confirmed.

New York city gate gas prices rallied almost a dime to the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $15.88 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained seven cents to the low-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.68 a barrel.
